results.citation: Eaton & Cole 1964, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 86(15):3157-3158
results.hardness_evidence: First synthesis of a Platonic hydrocarbon cage; ~695 kJ/mol angle strain (109.5deg tetrahedral carbons forced to 90deg cube vertices); specialized multi-step route from 2-cyclopentenone via base-mediated dimerization/rearrangement; derivatives historically hazardous (energetic-materials use).
results.name: cubane
results.why_it_slips: Fragment score is dominated by common small aliphatic CH2/CH substructures (frequent in the PubChem training corpus); the cage's high vertex/bond symmetry triggers the fingerprint-density symmetry bonus (score3, sascorer.py 'not in the original publication...to make highly symmetrical molecules easier to synthesise'); the algorithm has NO ring-strain term at all, so 682-695 kJ/mol of angle strain that drove decades of synthetic effort is structurally invisible to the score.

headline: 3/3 attack families executed. Family 1 (known-hard structures): 3/3 genuinely hard-to-synthesize strained-cage hydrocarbons score SA<6 (false feasible) -- cubane, prismane, dodecahedrane.
